$comment: Every control, panel, label and tab visible in the store screenshots, and the
UI-register affordance that proves the shipped app has it.
This file exists because a screenshot is a promise. The set before this one
showed an 'Invite to sign' button the app has never had; Apple's review
guideline 2.3.3 and Microsoft's policy 10.1.1 both ask for the app as it is,
and the house rule is stricter than either: everything the interface suggests
must work.
`shows` is a control the image shows and the app has. Its `affordance` is a
`kind:id` reference into docs/UI_REGISTER.md; tests/store-visuals-parity.test.ts
fails when that reference is gone from the register or has decayed to NO ACTION
or UNREACHABLE. A row with no reference must say why in `whyNoAffordance`.
`blocked` is a control the image shows and the app does NOT have, or shows
differently from the shipped shell. Each one names what the image claims,
what the app actually does, and the ticket where the owner decides between
changing the image and building the control. Nothing is uploaded, and no
derivative of that image enters docs/media/, while its list is non-empty.
Sources checked on 2026-09-08 against the shell at b22d536: the six Mac App
Store 2880x1800 renders and the six Microsoft Store 1920x1080 renders, which
carry the same six designs at a different aspect ratio.

Image ids are prefixed rather than bare digits on purpose. The register's proof walker probes test files for a quoted literal beside the token 'key', so a bare '1' in this file's test would have been counted as proof for the 1-8 mode shortcut -- a test credited with something it does not exercise, which is the exact failure the register exists to catch.
